metadata.climate_summary: Lisbon mid-August: hot dry 30-35C, virtually no rain, strong Atlantic sea breeze PM, heat-wave risk 14:00-17:00 block
metadata.tap_water: Potable — safe to drink from tap
metadata.tipping: Round up or 5-10% in restaurants; not mandatory

visa.rule: Schengen short-stay visa required for PH passport holders; apply at Portuguese consulate (Manila). 90-day maximum in any 180-day window.

places.name: Torre de Belém
places.description: UNESCO-listed Manueline limestone tower built 1516-1519 on the Tagus riverbank. Entry €6; advance tickets recommended. Climb is narrow — not suitable for claustrophobics.

places.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
places.description: Masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture, completed 1601. Houses tombs of Vasco da Gama and poet Luís de Camões. €12 entry; arrive before 10:00 to beat tour groups.

places.name: Praça do Comércio
places.description: Massive riverfront square framed by arcaded yellow buildings, opened post-1755 earthquake. Bronze equestrian statue of King José I at centre. Rua Augusta triumphal arch leads north. Free.

places.name: Tram 28 (Eléctrico 28)
places.description: Historic yellow wooden tram running through Alfama's steep alleys from Martim Moniz to Campo Ourique. Ride full route for €3.10 with Lisboa Viva card. Crowded midday — board at Graça terminus for a seat.
places.alt_search_query: Lisbon tram 28 historic yellow tram Alfama

places.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
places.description: Highest viewpoint in central Lisbon, overlooking São Jorge Castle, the Tagus, and Alfama rooftops. Less visited than Portas do Sol. Small chapel beside the terrace. Free, no facilities.
places.alt_search_query: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte Lisbon viewpoint Graça

places.name: LX Factory
places.description: Repurposed 19th-century textile factory turned creative hub: independent shops, bookstore Ler Devagar (with a swing), restaurants, weekend market Sunday 10:00-18:00. Free to enter; individual shops vary.
places.alt_search_query: LX Factory Alcântara Lisbon creative hub

places.name: Manteigaria – Fábrica de Pastéis de Nata
places.alt_search_query: Manteigaria pasteis de nata Chiado Lisbon
places.description: Standing-room pastry counter in Chiado producing fresh pastéis de nata every 15 minutes. €1.40 per tart, best eaten warm with cinnamon and icing sugar. Queue moves fast.

places.name: Pastéis de Belém
places.description: Original 1837 source of the custard tart recipe; the filling formula is a closely guarded secret. Takes on Blue Willow-pattern tiles. Price €1.40/tart. Queue can be 30min but moves quickly.

places.name: Tasca do Chico
places.alt_search_query: Tasca do Chico fado restaurant Bairro Alto Lisbon
places.description: Small wood-panelled tasca in Bairro Alto offering live fado music nightly at 20:00, free with your meal. Menu of petiscos (sharing plates): chouriço flambé, octopus salad, bacalhau. Reservation essential.

places.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
places.description: Curated food hall in the 1882 Mercado da Ribeira: 35+ stalls including starred-chef counters (Henrique Sá Pessoa), ginjinha bar, fresh seafood. Covered, air-conditioned. Open daily.

places.name: Bairro Alto Bar Crawl
places.description: Dense grid of narrow streets (Rua da Atalaia, Rua do Norte, Rua Diário de Notícias) packed with independent bars. Bars open doors from 22:00; street drinking with plastic cups is tolerated. Budget €3-5 per beer.

places.name: Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho)
places.description: 700m street painted bright pink, formerly a red-light district, now a lineup of late-night bars and clubs. Bicaense, Pensão Amor, and Sol e Pesca are anchors. Heats up after midnight.
places.alt_search_query: Pink Street Rua Nova do Carvalho Lisbon nightlife

places.name: MAAT – Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
places.description: Contemporary art and architecture museum by Amanda Levete; wave-shaped white tiles on riverside. Collection covers media art and digital installations. Entry €11, riverside terrace free. Air-conditioned.
places.alt_search_query: MAAT Museum Art Architecture Technology Lisbon Belem

places.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
places.description: Encyclopedic collection from Egyptian antiquities to Renoir, Rembrandt, and Lalique glass, assembled by oil magnate Calouste Gulbenkian. Entry €10; gardens included. One of Europe's best-kept museum secrets.
places.alt_search_query: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum Lisbon art collection

places.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
places.alt_search_query: Cervejaria Ramiro seafood restaurant Lisbon Intendente
places.description: Lisbon's most famous beerhouse serving piri-piri prawns, clams in garlic-wine, and grilled lobster since 1956. Queue outside or book. Finish with a prego sandwich. Budget €40-60pp with drinks.

places.name: Castelo de São Jorge
places.description: Moorish hilltop castle dominating Lisbon's skyline; panoramic views over the city and Tagus estuary. Entry €15; includes archaeological site and peacocks in the grounds. Go early to avoid heat and crowds.
places.alt_search_query: Castelo de São Jorge Lisbon Alfama castle

places.name: Sintra Day Trip (Pena Palace)
places.description: Romantic 19th-century hilltop palace in vivid yellow-and-red Romanticist style, 40min by train from Rossio. UNESCO World Heritage site. Entry €14; combined ticket with park €17. Go early — crowds surge by 11:00.
places.alt_search_query: Pena Palace Sintra Portugal Romanticist palace

places.name: Bairro Alto Hotel Spa
places.alt_search_query: Bairro Alto Hotel spa Chiado Lisbon wellness
places.description: Boutique spa at Bairro Alto Hotel with mosaic tile pool, steam room, and Portuguese cork-oil treatments. Massages from €90 for 50min. Advance booking required.

places.name: Museu do Fado
places.description: Two-floor museum tracing fado's evolution from 19th-century Alfama taverns to UNESCO heritage status. Listening booths with headphones, vintage instruments, photographs. Entry €5.
places.alt_search_query: Museu do Fado Lisbon Alfama fado museum

places.name: Elevador de Santa Justa
places.description: Wrought-iron neo-Gothic elevator designed by Raoul Mesnier du Ponsard (1902), connecting Baixa to Carmo. €5.30 single. Upper terrace offers rooftop view of Rossio. Worth it for the architecture alone.
places.alt_search_query: Santa Justa Lift Elevador Lisbon Baixa

places.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
places.description: Housed in a 16th-century Manueline convent, the world's only museum dedicated to azulejo (blue-and-white tile). 20,000-piece panorama of Lisbon pre-1755 earthquake. Entry €5. A/C.
places.alt_search_query: Museu Nacional do Azulejo Lisbon tile museum Beato

risk_flags: PH passport holders must obtain Schengen type-C visa via Portuguese consulate in Manila before travel — apply 6-8 weeks early.
Lisbon August averages 35C+ with occasional 40C+ heat waves; outdoor activities should avoid 13:00-17:00; stay hydrated with 2L/day minimum.
Tram 28 and Alfama tourist streets are active pickpocket zones; use inner pockets, no rear-pocket wallets, split cash.
Pena Palace reaches capacity by 11:00 in August; pre-book timed entry and arrive before 09:15 or accept 45min queue.
Turkish Airlines connection at Istanbul; IST is a large airport — allow 2hr minimum transit buffer for MNL connection.

practical_info: Currency
Euro (EUR). ATMs widely available — use Multibanco network. Avoid airport ATMs (high fees); use city Multibanco for better rates.
Cash vs Card
Cards accepted almost everywhere in Lisbon proper; carry €30-50 cash for taxis, markets, small tascas. Some Alfama tascas cash-only.
SIM / eSIM
EU eSIM from Airalo (Orange Portugal or NOS) from €12 for 15 days, 10GB. Activate on arrival. Alternatively buy NOS or MEO prepaid at airport.
Metro + Tram
Lisbon Viva card (€0.50) + Zapping credit works on Metro, trams, buses. Single fare ~€1.40. 24hr unlimited pass €6.60.
Taxis + Rideshare
Uber, Bolt, and Freenow all operate. Bolt typically cheapest. Avoid unmarked taxis in Alfama tourist areas — ask for metered fare.
Siesta Culture
Most sit-down restaurants close 15:00-19:30. Eating window: lunch 12:00-14:30, dinner 19:30-23:30. Lisbon eats late.
Heat Advisory
August heat waves 35-42C are common. Carry minimum 1.5L water. Avoid sun exposure 13:00-17:00. Wear light linen or breathable synthetics.
Language
Portuguese. English widely spoken in tourist areas; less so in outer neighbourhoods. Learn obrigado (thank you) and por favor.
Safety
Lisbon is generally safe. Main risks: pickpockets on Tram 28 and Alfama; occasional bag-snatching near Praça do Comércio. Keep bags front-facing.
Tap Water
Potable — safe to drink. Lisbon tap water has slight chlorine taste; many locals buy mineral water anyway. Bring refillable bottle.
Power Plug
Type F (Schuko) — PH plugs (Type A) will not fit directly. Buy a Type A to F adaptor in Manila or at LIS airport (€5-8). Voltage 230V/50Hz.
Tipping
10% appreciated in restaurants (not mandatory); round up for coffee. Tipping culture is lighter than USA or UK.
Public Toilets
Scarce outside major monuments. Use café toilets — buy an espresso (€0.80) to justify use. Jerónimos and MAAT have clean facilities.
Pharmacies
Farmácia widespread; marked with green cross. Will dispense paracetamol, ibuprofen, sunscreen without prescription.
Emergency
112 universal (police, ambulance, fire). Hospital São José is the main central hospital; private CUF Descobertas has English-speaking staff.

indoor_bank.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
indoor_bank.notes: Masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture, completed 1601. Houses tombs of Vasco da Gama and poet Luís de Camões. €12 entry; arrive before 10:00 to beat tour groups.

indoor_bank.name: LX Factory
indoor_bank.notes: Repurposed 19th-century textile factory turned creative hub: independent shops, bookstore Ler Devagar (with a swing), restaurants, weekend market Sunday 10:00-18:00. Free to enter; individual shops va

indoor_bank.name: Manteigaria – Fábrica de Pastéis de Nata
indoor_bank.notes: Standing-room pastry counter in Chiado producing fresh pastéis de nata every 15 minutes. €1.40 per tart, best eaten warm with cinnamon and icing sugar. Queue moves fast.

indoor_bank.name: Pastéis de Belém
indoor_bank.notes: Original 1837 source of the custard tart recipe; the filling formula is a closely guarded secret. Takes on Blue Willow-pattern tiles. Price €1.40/tart. Queue can be 30min but moves quickly.

indoor_bank.name: Tasca do Chico
indoor_bank.notes: Small wood-panelled tasca in Bairro Alto offering live fado music nightly at 20:00, free with your meal. Menu of petiscos (sharing plates): chouriço flambé, octopus salad, bacalhau. Reservation essent

indoor_bank.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
indoor_bank.notes: Curated food hall in the 1882 Mercado da Ribeira: 35+ stalls including starred-chef counters (Henrique Sá Pessoa), ginjinha bar, fresh seafood. Covered, air-conditioned. Open daily.

indoor_bank.name: MAAT – Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
indoor_bank.notes: Contemporary art and architecture museum by Amanda Levete; wave-shaped white tiles on riverside. Collection covers media art and digital installations. Entry €11, riverside terrace free. Air-condition

indoor_bank.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
indoor_bank.notes: Encyclopedic collection from Egyptian antiquities to Renoir, Rembrandt, and Lalique glass, assembled by oil magnate Calouste Gulbenkian. Entry €10; gardens included. One of Europe's best-kept museum s

indoor_bank.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
indoor_bank.notes: Lisbon's most famous beerhouse serving piri-piri prawns, clams in garlic-wine, and grilled lobster since 1956. Queue outside or book. Finish with a prego sandwich. Budget €40-60pp with drinks.

indoor_bank.name: Bairro Alto Hotel Spa
indoor_bank.notes: Boutique spa at Bairro Alto Hotel with mosaic tile pool, steam room, and Portuguese cork-oil treatments. Massages from €90 for 50min. Advance booking required.

indoor_bank.name: Museu do Fado
indoor_bank.notes: Two-floor museum tracing fado's evolution from 19th-century Alfama taverns to UNESCO heritage status. Listening booths with headphones, vintage instruments, photographs. Entry €5.

indoor_bank.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
indoor_bank.notes: Housed in a 16th-century Manueline convent, the world's only museum dedicated to azulejo (blue-and-white tile). 20,000-piece panorama of Lisbon pre-1755 earthquake. Entry €5. A/C.

transport_tips: Lisboa Viva card (€0.50) + Zapping credit is the correct city transit setup — works on Metro, Tram, Bus, Elevadores.
Tram 15E is the fastest way to Belém; departs Praça da Figueira every 10-12min.
Metro has 4 lines (Yellow/Blue/Green/Red); Red Line connects airport to Alameda interchange.
Bolt and Uber are cheaper than taxis (€3-8 for most inner-city rides). Avoid TukTuks for transport — tourist pricing.
CP trains (Comboios de Portugal) serve Sintra (Rossio line) and Cascais (Cais do Sodré line). Zapping card valid.
Alfama and Bairro Alto are pedestrian-first; streets too narrow for rideshare drop-off in many spots — walk last 200m.
Night buses (Carris) operate after Metro closes (01:00). Night Bus 759 connects Baixa to Bairro Alto.
accommodation_recommendation: Bairro Alto is the optimal base: walkable to Chiado, LX nightlife, Time Out Market, and Santa Justa. Mid-range recommendation: Hotel do Chiado (rooftop castle views, €140-200/night). Budget: Generator Lisbon Graça or Casa de São Mamede. For honeymoon/splurge: Bairro Alto Hotel (5 stars, €380+).
